basis: Defined by intellectual disability, speech and motor delay, and brain abnormalities; cardiac abnormalities are less frequent.
Follicular skin atrophy and cutaneous basal cell carcinoma define this condition.
Leukodystrophy with progressive ataxia and pyramidal dysfunction plus defining dental agenesis; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.
Umbrella for congenital nervous system abnormalities; additional organs are subtype-specific.
Acquired reading impairment from cerebral cortical and white-matter lesions; no intrinsic eye disease.
CEP164-related nephronophthisis; retinal degeneration affects 6/7 patients. Neurologic abnormalities occur in only 1/7.
Ulcerative inflammation of oral mucosa; no specific infectious or autoimmune mechanism is established for the umbrella.
Hereditary optic atrophy; intellectual disability and ataxia each occur in 2/6 patients (~33%), supporting neurologic involvement.
Nonsyndromic inherited hearing loss; hearing impairment reported in 5/5 patients.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis in 9/9 and sinusitis in 11/13; recurrent infections are secondary to impaired clearance.
Defining muscular torticollis, keloids and renal dysplasia; reproductive anomalies have no axis. Additional vascular or neurologic damage lacks frequency evidence.
Repeated acute inflammation of the exocrine pancreas; remote organ injury is variable and not established in at least 30%.
Unilateral congenital skeletal malformation of the foot.
Hereditary susceptibility specifically to cutaneous melanoma; no additional organ damage is established.
Storage myopathy and cardiomyopathy define infantile Pompe; cerebral white-matter lesions 80-99%; macroglossia 30-79% omitted by cap; hepatomegaly alone lacks functional damage.
Isolated congenital absence of a male reproductive structure; no represented organ axis.
Disorder of lipoprotein metabolism; atherosclerotic disease is a separate downstream condition, not direct involvement.
PLG angioedema characteristically affects facial subcutis and tongue/oral mucosa; bradykinin-mediated rather than immune deficiency. Other organ damage is not established as common.
Benign fibroelastic neoplasm of deep connective tissue, typically beneath the scapula.
Congenital eyelid and globe malformation; covering skin is part of the ocular defect, without a separate skin disorder.
Plasmodium vivax infects erythrocytes; severe extrahematologic organ injury is a minority complication.
Adenoviral infection directly inflames the cornea and conjunctiva.
Skeletal dysplasia with vertebral abnormalities and severe dwarfism; glaucoma is a defining component of the named syndrome.
Neoplasm originating in pineal parenchymal cells; the pineal is both a brain structure and an endocrine gland.
Malignant neoplasm involving the kidney; no additional organ involvement is inherent across this umbrella.
